summary: Masaaki Hattori is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta, working with Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, Atsuuji Ashikaga, Gadjin Nagao, and V. P. Limaye, and taught at Kyoto University (1961–1988).

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1967). He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).
Masaaki Nohnin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and later professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.
Masaaki Tsuchiya works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1980–1989) and held a post at Senshu University around 1997.

Masaharu Anesaki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo, Kiel, and with scholars including Deussen and Oldenberg. He served as a director and library head at the University of Tokyo (1904; 1923–1934).

Masaharu Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who earned a doctorate from Tokyo University of Education (1977). He taught at Ibaraki University (1977) and became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba in 2006.

Masahide Mori works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his MA at Nagoya University and his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later serving as assistant professor (~1999–2006) and professor (from ~2006) at Kanazawa University.
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1974) and subsequently served there as an assistant professor (~1982–1992).

Masahiro Inami specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University (~1985–1991) and has held teaching posts at Tokyo Gakugei University from around 1992, becoming a teacher there by ~2006.

Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1948–1953). He served as professor and chair of religious studies and history of religion at Tohoku University (~1968–1985).

Masahiro Shimoda specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (PhD 1993) and Delhi University, served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023), and joined Musashino University in 2023.
Masahiro Takano is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a librarian in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University (~1968–1972). He later served as head of the department of the History of Japanese Philosophy at Kyoto University (~2002–2014).

Masakazu Tanaka works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and earned his PhD at the London School of Economics, later serving as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and vice president at the Professional Institute of International Fashion (2019).

Masako Keta is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied under Yoshinori Takeuchi at Kyoto University. She held positions at Kanazawa University (1988, 1998) before serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).
Masamichi Asukai was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He completed his studies at Kyoto University (~1952–1956) and later held an academic post there from around 1978 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University, Kyoto University (D.Litt. 1985) under Gadjin Nagao, and taught at Kyoto Sangyo University (professor 1981) and Otani University (professor 1997).
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under the doctoral supervision of Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and assistant professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an assistant professor post at Osaka University (attested 2012) and served as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).
